text:
kara: Hey team — quick one. I realized I haven't maxed my 401(k) catch-up for 2026 and want to push a big catch-up deferral on my final payroll before a vendor migration. Is that possible, or will migration block last-minute deferrals?

miriam: You can usually submit a supplemental deferral request but it MUST hit payroll before the migration cutoff. Migration window 2026-11-08 -> 2026-11-12; final pay run that would capture corrections is 2026-11-07.

rex: Also watch contribution limits — catch-up applies only if you're 50+. Year-to-date contributions + requested catch-up must not exceed IRS limits (elective deferral limit + catch-up). If you exceed, excess contributions are taxable and need correction.

opsbot: PlanAdmin note: "Payroll-initiated corrections for elective deferrals may be processed as an off-cycle if submitted before migration cutoff. After migration, off-cycle processing may be delayed and could miss calendar-year posting deadlines. Participant is responsible for monitoring year-to-date totals."

kara: I'm 51, so catch-up applies. I want to push $7k catch-up on the Nov last check. How do I request it?

payroll: Email payroll@redwood with subject "SUPP_DEFERRAL - kara" including: Employee name, SS last 4, Amount, Paydate to apply (include pay run date), and signature. Submit by EOD 2026-11-05 to be safe. If it's a manual off-cycle, we'll need manager approval too.

miriam: Also check HSA/FSA interplay — if you had pre-tax HSA contributions planned for that payroll, ordering matters because some systems reconcile in the order: 401k deferral -> HSA -> taxes. If changing amounts, ask payroll to provide projected YTD with the change so you don't accidentally go over limits.

rex: If the migration causes posting delays and the catch-up hits next calendar year, you'll lose the 2026 tax benefit. Rare but true — we recommend ACH to PlanAdmin? (not for deferrals, only for loan/payments).

opsbot: Automated: PlanAdmin processing hours are paused during vendor migrations. Submit all payroll-affecting requests 48 hours before cutoff per policy.

kara: Thanks. Is there a form for supplemental deferral?

payroll: There's a one-page PDF on the benefits portal called "Supplemental Deferral Request". Fill, sign, and attach to the payroll email. We'll run the off-cycle if possible; otherwise we'll apply to the last regular run.

miriam: Quick checklist for you @kara: 1) Download the PDF. 2) Calculate YTD contributions + requested catch-up (we can help). 3) Send to payroll@redwood by 11/05 with subject line above and cc your manager. 4) We'll confirm posting before migration starts.

kara: Perfect — sending numbers now. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

rex: One more FYI: if you hit the limit accidentally, correction involves removing excess and issuing Form 1099-R. It's messier than getting it right the first time.

opsbot: Reminder: last_action_deadline=2026-11-05.
